question: Does Baleta and Baleta (2016) provide reliable Palanan species-by-site or seasonal occurrence evidence, or a historical landing-name lead only?

source.citation: Baleta, A. N., Jr., & Baleta, F. N. (2016). Species composition of marine food fishes at Palanan, Isabela as influenced by seasonal variation. International Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Studies, 4(3), 414–420.
source.publisherMetadata: The PDF first-page header gives 2016, 4(3), pages 414–420 and a copyright notice; its running header instead prints 4(2), so issue metadata conflicts within the document.
source.authorsAffiliation: Both authors are listed with the Institute of Fisheries, Isabela State University.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The article displays © 2016 IJFAS. No item-specific open license or permission to redistribute its list, figures, or reported photos was verified.

retrievalFollowUp.publisherDirectPdf: The publisher-hosted PDF could not be retrieved as a file through direct fetch; browser/web open was blocked or restricted. A search provider returned indexed text from the publisher PDF, and a Doczz transcription was also readable.
retrievalFollowUp.indexedText: The indexed extraction exposes the abstract, methods and table text. The Doczz transcription agrees on major printed labels, but it is a secondary text mirror, not a page-image check. Table 1 name/common-name columns and Table 2 season marks are reflowed; individual row associations and checkmarks are not considered visually verified.
retrievalFollowUp.pageImageReview: Not completed: no PDF page images were retrieved. Table layout, Figure 1 station map and the paper's claimed fish photo documentation remain unreviewed.
retrievalFollowUp.disposition: Use the surfaced text only to document selected source conflicts. Do not transcribe the 74-name list, normalize spellings, infer seasonal presence, or treat the extracted table as a verified checklist. Seek an author, Isabela State University, journal or library scan before any row-level crosswalk.

secondaryTextMirror.purpose: Compared the readable transcription with the publisher-indexed extraction to identify access and text-reflow limitations; not treated as an independent scientific source or page-image check.

conflicts: The abstract prints Acanthurus lineatus; Table 1 prints Acanthurus lineathus and the extracted Table 2 prints Acanthunus lineathus. Do not select or normalize one spelling from the text extraction.

The extracted Table 1 text appears to align Cheilopogon melanurus with the common name Atlantic Flyingfish. FAO identifies that English name and describes a western Atlantic distribution; this is a material biogeographic flag for the Palanan attribution, not a confirmed misidentification. The table pairing still needs page-image review.

The extracted Table 1 text appears to align Istiophorus albicans with Atlantic Sailfish. ITIS treats I. albicans as a junior synonym of I. platypterus, while an ICCAT 2024 paper summarizes genetic evidence for a single worldwide I. platypterus and documents continuing naming differences. Preserve the source label and taxonomic disagreement; do not use the Atlantic common name alone to reject the Palanan report. The table pairing still needs page-image review.

The extracted Table 1 repeats Lutjanus decussates with different Filipino-name cells; the available text does not establish whether this is a duplicate row, transcription issue, or distinct vernacular observation.
indexedTableAudit.seasonTableDisposition: Do not convert the April-versus-October checkmarks into presence/absence assertions until the table image and row alignment are reviewed.

reportedScope.locality: Four fish landing stations in Palanan, Isabela: Dicotcotan, Sabang, Culasi and Dimolid.
reportedScope.methodAsReported: Ocular inspection and interviews with 40 fishers and/or vendors (10 per landing area); the article says the interviews occurred at the onset of summer (April) and rainy season (October), and that photo documentation was gathered.
reportedScope.identificationAsReported: The paper names field guides for Tayabas Bay and Palawan and FishBase for final verification. The accessible article does not identify vouchers or provide a verifiable photo-to-taxon archive.
reportedScope.temporalLimit: The article does not state the calendar year or exact dates for the April and October sampling/interviews. It does not establish annual or current presence.
reportedScope.tableScope: Table 1 is described as a pooled list with scientific, English, Filipino and Paranan names. Table 2 is a pooled summer-versus-rainy-season comparison, but its text extraction does not preserve reliable checkmark-to-name alignment. The article does not provide a verified species-by-landing-site matrix or capture coordinates.

conflictsAndLimits: The paper prints 7°3′32″ N, 122°25′47″ E as the study-area coordinate. This is held as suspect for the stated Palanan/Isabela locality and is not used to georeference any record; the article gives no corrected station coordinates.

The abstract and extracted tables disagree on the printed Acanthurus spelling (lineatus / lineathus / Acanthunus lineathus). Additional table labels have common-name, duplicate-row or biogeographic flags. See indexedTableAudit; no label is normalized.

The extracted table text appears to pair Cheilopogon melanurus with Atlantic Flyingfish, while the FAO account gives a western Atlantic distribution. This raises a source-identification or locality flag that needs voucher, photo or author clarification; the table pairing itself is not image-verified and it is not silently treated as a false record.

The extracted table text appears to pair Istiophorus albicans with Atlantic Sailfish. Taxonomic authorities differ on whether I. albicans is a separate Atlantic species or a synonym of the worldwide I. platypterus; preserve that disagreement and do not infer the Philippine report is impossible from the common name. The extracted table pairing needs page-image review.

The extracted Table 1 repeats Lutjanus decussates with different Filipino-name cells. Without the page image, do not assume whether this is a duplicate, a transcription problem or a vernacular-name detail.
The paper says 74 species; its results report 52 genera, 37 families and 9 orders. These are source claims, not an independently checked count or an app checklist.
Landing-site records describe fish reported or seen at market/landing contexts, not confirmed capture coordinates or occurrence inside the adjacent municipal-water polygon.

The paper does not specify the sampling year, survey effort beyond the interviews, fisher sampling frame, catch-landing inclusion rules, vouchers, station coordinates, or reproducible species-by-site counts.
The article's season labels and discussion use broader seasonal periods without supplying exact sample dates; do not turn the pooled April/October comparison into a monthly calendar or season rule.

No source-specific license was verified. Public access to the PDF is not treated as permission for public-app reproduction. The paper's claimed photo documentation was not used as a Bangwit image source.

disposition.sourceUse: Research-only historical Palanan landing and vernacular-name lead; consider for a later manually checked taxonomic crosswalk, not for present-day species occurrence.

nextAction: Continue searching non-government academic/library/author copies for a page-image-readable PDF and ask the authors or Isabela State University to clarify the table labels, photo/voucher trail, and coordinates if a public contact is available. Meanwhile, keep the complete list, seasonal marks, map and reported photos out of app data. A future crosswalk may examine only selected labels against authoritative taxonomy after the original table image is checked. Keep this paper separate from the 2017 Isabela-wide landing study and do not sum their aggregate counts.

sources.supports: Publisher-indexed article text for the four Palanan landing stations, interview/ocular method, April/October labels, paper-reported aggregate counts, identification method, printed coordinate, and selected conflicting scientific/common-name labels. Direct PDF fetch/page images were unavailable; table layout and seasonal checkmark alignment remain unverified.

FAO species account for Cheilopogon melanurus identifies the FAO English name Atlantic flyingfish and describes its western Atlantic range; this supports flagging the Palanan table's name/locality pair for review, not rejecting a catch record without voucher evidence.
ITIS taxonomic entry for Istiophorus albicans lists Atlantic Sailfish as a common name and Istiophorus platypterus as its valid name, reflecting one current treatment of the sailfish name.

2024 ICCAT scientific paper reviews the Atlantic/Indo-Pacific sailfish naming question and summarizes genetic evidence for a single worldwide Istiophorus platypterus; cited to preserve the disagreement around the source table's I. albicans label, not to identify its specimen.
